patch.value: Own the TOON 4.0.0 major upgrade separately from routine dependency refreshes. Upstream declares no Node engine floor, but the major storage codec must prove byte-level item/history compatibility, strict decode/encode behavior, migration safety, and all release gates before adoption.

TOON 4 is evaluated against canonical item files and history replay; encode/decode and migration fixtures remain lossless; Node 22/24/26 and Bun installed consumers pass; the upgrade is adopted or explicitly rejected with upstream evidence.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Dependency-drift sweep 2026-07-26 (live npm query, whole manifest).

Runtime and toolchain drift, current -> latest:

| package | current | latest | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| @toon-format/toon | 2.3.1 | 4.1.0 | **two majors** |
| npm-package-arg | 13.0.2 | 14.0.0 | one major |
| typescript | 6.0.3 | 7.0.2 | one major |
| @sentry/node | 10.67.0 | 10.68.0 | patch |
| typebox | 1.3.7 | 1.3.8 | patch |

pnpm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities at every severity (info/low/moderate/
high/critical all zero), and GitHub Dependabot shows 0 open alerts, so none of
this is a security exposure. It is a maintenance-currency finding.

Why the TOON row is the one that matters here rather than the TypeScript row:
TOON is the default output encoding for the entire agent-facing surface
(output_default: "toon"), so this dependency sits on every read path an agent
touches. Published majors are 0, 1, 2 and 4 across 20 versions — the project is
pinned on 2.x while the registry has moved to 4.x, and there is no 3.x, so the
upgrade is a single two-major step rather than an incremental walk.

This also intersects an open correctness defect on the same encoder: GH-747
(pm-hybj) reports that the TOON encoder emits a quoted notes[] scalar its own
decoder rejects, making valid tracked items unreadable — the same failure family
as pm-iqgj (closed), where the strict decoder mis-parsed bracketed tokens and 16
item files had to be recovered. Evaluating whether 4.x already fixes the
encoder/decoder asymmetry is therefore part of this item's scope and may reduce
it, not just a compatibility exercise.

No re-file: this evidence is recorded here because pm-5cgm2z already owns the
TOON 4 evaluation and item-format migration.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Link the TOON 4 evaluation to the open encoder/decoder round-trip defect and the closed recovery of 16 unreadable item files, both on the same encoder.
